back: Treating a genetic disorder by inserting a functional allele into a patient's cells.
Somatic: body cells, not inherited. Germ-line: gametes or early embryo, inherited by descendants.
Bone marrow stem cells given the ADA allele by a retro/lentiviral vector ex vivo, then returned.

front: Gene therapy for Leber congenital amaurosis
back: AAV carrying the normal allele injected under the retina; non-dividing retinal cells keep expressing it.
Short-lived effects, immune responses, insertion near oncogenes, poor delivery, high cost.

front: Why germ-line therapy is not permitted in most countries
back: Inherited by future generations who cannot consent; errors inherited; unknown long-term effects; enhancement fears.

front: Why recessive conditions suit gene therapy
back: Adding one working allele supplies the missing protein; a dominant faulty allele would still act.
Ex vivo: cells removed, treated, returned. In vivo: vector delivered directly into the body tissue.
